sql:
SELECT
  o.month_label AS month,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_qualifying,
  ROUND(AVG(f.shipped_at::date - o.placed_at::date), 2) AS avg_processing_days,
  ROUND(AVG(f.delivered_at::date - f.shipped_at::date), 2) AS avg_transit_days,
  ROUND(AVG(f.delivered_at::date - o.placed_at::date), 2) AS avg_total_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN (f.delivered_at::date - o.placed_at::date) <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days_total
FROM (
  SELECT orders.id, orders.placed_at, cd.month_label
  FROM orders
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = orders.placed_at::date
  WHERE orders.status = 'fulfilled'
    AND orders.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND orders.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
) o
JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
WHERE f.shipped_at IS NOT NULL
  AND f.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
  AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments f2 WHERE f2.order_id = o.id) = 1
GROUP BY o.month_label
ORDER BY o.month_label
note: Scoped to fulfilled orders placed in 2025 with exactly one fulfillment row that has both shipped_at and delivered_at set, per the single-fulfillment simplifying rule. Day diffs use date-level subtraction (whole days); I could not verify in the empty dry-run schema whether avg_total_days materially deviates from avg_processing_days + avg_transit_days, so please sanity-check that once real data runs.
